title: Patch: the fuzz regression corpus keeps the start its seed drew, not only its decks
thread:
**Issue #4062 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4062: Patch: the fuzz regression corpus keeps the start its seed drew, not only its decks
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Today a kept fuzz failure pins only its seed and its two decks, and the regression run always replays it as a plain game from scratch. But most fuzz games do not start from scratch: they start with pre-dealt hands, rebuilt end-of-game boards, glitch boards, or as dungeon fights with damaged heroes and marked decks. If a failure is found in one of those games, there is nowhere to keep the start it came from, so the checked-in regression replays a different game that passes without ever touching the failing shape. After this change, pinning a failure keeps the start too, and the regression run replays the game that actually failed.

## Why

- `START_STATE_SHARE` is 0.5 and `RUN_START_SHARE` is 0.15 (`crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`): well over half of all fuzz seeds run from a dealt, last-boards, glitch-boards, or dungeon-fight start, in both 1v1 waves. Any failure on those shares is unpinnable today.
- `replay_record` replays every record through `GameSetup::plain`, with the comment that the plain start is \"the one every kept failure was found from\". That assumption holds only until the first non-plain failure needs pinning; the day it breaks, the corpus silently replays the wrong game.
- The boards themselves drift: `manufactured_board` shuffles `BOARD_POOL`, which is built from the live catalog, so a later card changes what a seed draws — the same drift the module docs already admit for decks (`FUZZ_POOL`). Re-drawing boards from the seed at regress time would not rebuild the failing boards; they must be pinned literally, exactly as decks already are.
- A dungeon-start failure cannot even pass the record lint: its decks hold `RUN_START_DECK_MIN` to `RUN_START_DECK_MAX` cards, not `DECK_SIZE` or `EARLIER_DECK_SIZE`, and its handicaps and deck marks have no field at all.
- Not covered elsewhere: #4058 and #4057 deepen what the monitor checks per step; this is about which game the corpus replays. #1363 (a Duos corpus) was rejected, so this stays inside the existing 1v1 scope the corpus README already claims.

## Proposal

- Extend `CorpusRecord` with optional pinned start inputs (all `#[serde(default)]` so the nine existing records keep reading under `deny_unknown_fields`): the start kind, and the drawn inputs the failure report already knows — dealt seats, both manufactured boards, or the dungeon fight's handicaps and deck marks — plus whether the seed drew the endings channel.
- Print those inputs in the failure report next to the existing `start:`, `handicaps:`, `marks:` and deck lines, in copy-pasteable record shape, so pinning one is mechanical.
- Replay records through the pinned start (`create_options`-equivalent in `replay_record`) instead of `GameSetup::plain`, and extend the record lint to the pinned inputs (board ids held to the live catalog, run decks to the run size range), reusing the existing `retired` rule when a pinned id leaves the catalog.
- Update `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md` (which today documents the plain-start limitation as fact) and add one record exercising the new fields, e.g. by pinning a dealt/last-boards seed.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`: `CorpusRecord`, `lint_record`, `replay_record`, the failure `report` lines; SPEC §9.3 (replay/fold inputs), §10.7 (the fuzz policy), R417/R678 (last boards, Glitch boards), R433 (dealt seats), R2702000/R2922000/R2922001 (dungeon starts), R1705003 (deck sizes).
- `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md` and one new record file; the existing `fuzz_regression_corpus` test covers the run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A record pinning a non-plain start (boards or dungeon inputs) replays through that start under `cargo jackioh fuzz --regress`, and fails there when its bug is reintroduced.
- [ ] The nine existing records read unchanged and still pass.
- [ ] A record whose pinned board id left the catalog is retired by the lint, never edited, as deck ids already are.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` (incl. `fuzz_regression_corpus`), `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Size and risks

- Medium: one struct, a few report lines, one replay path, lint rules, docs, one record. No engine, rule, or spec change; no new CI job (`rust` already runs the regress test).
- Risk: records grow (two boards of card ids); mitigated by keeping one file per record, as today. Explicitly out of scope: handicapped-wave and Duos records (Duos corpus was rejected in #1363) and any change to how the waves draw starts.

---

## Plan

_Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43981401087)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Allow each 1v1 fuzz corpus record to preserve the exact start that produced its failure: start kind, dealt seats or literal boards, dungeon handicaps and deck marks, and the endings-channel flag. Regression replay must use supplied pinned inputs, legacy records must retain their plain-start behavior through serde defaults, and lint/reporting/documentation must make adding and retiring pinned records mechanical.

## Files to touch

| Path | Status | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` | change | Extend `StartKind`/`CorpusRecord`, report pinned fields, lint start inputs, and replay from literal `CreateGameOptions`; add focused tests. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | Update the `fuzz --regress` command contract to say starts and the endings channel are pinned with decks. |
| `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md` | change | Document the optional pinned-start fields, validation/retirement rules, and exact replay behavior instead of the plain-start limitation. |
| `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/seed-3760-v0.4.12c.json` | change | Pin the historical plain-start failure's true endings-channel flag and remove its obsolete mismatch note. |
| `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/seed-8-v0.4.12d.json` | change | Pin the historical failure's dealt start (`p1` and `p2`) and false endings-channel flag, then remove the now-obsolete statement that regress replays it plain. |

Do not touch `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/run`, any app, the spec notes, or forbidden `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, and `.claude/` paths. The implementation is governed by SPEC §9.3 and §10.7 and rulings R417/R564/R678 (literal rebuildable boards), R433 (dealt seats), R180/R184/R2702000/R2922000/R2922001 (dungeon handicaps, deck sizes, and marks), and R1705003 (recorded-game deck sizes); it makes no new rules decision or ruling.

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, make `StartKind` public and derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize` with kebab-case names; implement `Default` as `Plain`. Extend `CorpusRecord` with camel-case fields `start: StartKind`, `dealt: Option<Vec<PlayerId>>`, `last_boards: Option<LastBoardInput>`, `glitch_boards: Option<LastBoardInput>`, `handicaps: Option<PerPlayerOpt<Handicap>>`, `deck_marks: Option<PerPlayerOpt<Vec<DeckMark>>>`, and `endings: bool`; put `#[serde(default)]` on every new field so every record omitting them still means plain/no-channel. Import `LastBoardInput`, `SetupKind`, and `validate_setup` from `jackioh_engine`. Update the module comments “The regression corpus,” “Starting states,” “Dungeon-fight starts,” and “The endings channel,” plus the `StartKind::Plain` and `GameSetup::plain` comments, so none still claims corpus replay is always plain or channel-free.
2. Add `CorpusRecord::create_options(&self) -> CreateGameOptions`, using `GameSetup::plain(self.seed).stream("")`, cloned pinned decks and all literal engine inputs. Extract `fold_args_from_options(options: &CreateGameOptions, log: Vec<Action>) -> FoldArgs`; make `GameSetup::fold_args` delegate to it. Add `play_game_with_options`, `check_replay_with_options`, `check_serial_restart_with_options`, and `run_seed_with_options` beside their current functions: the current functions remain wrappers that call `GameSetup::create_options`, while `replay_record` creates a `GameSetup` with `recorded: true`, `start: record.start`, and `endings: record.endings`, then calls `run_seed_with_options` with `record.create_options()`. This keeps the same play, termination, replay, checkpoint, invariant, probe, and growth checks while ensuring initial creation, full fold, and checkpoint prefix all consume the same pinned options. Never redraw a corpus board or dungeon input from `BOARD_POOL`, `FUZZ_POOL`, or `start-inputs-`.
3. Add `endings: bool` to `Failure`, populate it from `GameSetup` in `run_seed_with_options`, and update the file's test fixtures. Replace `Failure::run_start_note` with `Failure::start_options`, reconstructing the exact failing wave/setup with the stored `start` and `endings`, then use it in `report`. After the existing human-readable `start:`, `handicaps:`, and `marks:` lines, print copy-pasteable JSON record lines for `"start"`, the one applicable input (`"dealt"`, `"lastBoards"`, `"glitchBoards"`, or `"handicaps"` plus `"deckMarks"`), and `"endings"` as `true` or `false`. Keep the existing deck lines and existing `--json` keys stable; print literal board entries, not a seed recipe.
4. In `lint_record`, validate the new shape before replay. Require only the inputs belonging to `start` (none for plain, `dealt` for dealt, `lastBoards` for last-boards, `glitchBoards` for glitch-boards, and both `handicaps` and `deckMarks` for run), reject conflicting/omitted inputs, and require a dealt list to equal one of `DEALT_SEATS`. For `Run`, require each deck length independently in inclusive `RUN_START_DECK_MIN..=RUN_START_DECK_MAX`; for other starts retain matching `DECK_SIZE`/`EARLIER_DECK_SIZE` decks. After `preview_every_set`, call `validate_setup(&record.create_options(), &CATALOG, SetupKind::Recorded)` to validate live records' deck ids, handicap sizes/values, tokens, and marks. For every pinned board entry, accept a catalog id or a fused id for which `subsystems::last_boards::rebuildable_from_id` is true; otherwise emit the existing “mark the record retired, never edit” class of error. Preserve the current rule that non-empty `retired` bypasses catalog-dependent deck/board validation while seed/version/found, sizes, duplicates, and start-field consistency still lint.
5. Pin the two checked-in records whose `found` text already documents lost setup. In `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/seed-8-v0.4.12d.json`, add `"start": "dealt"`, `"dealt": ["p1", "p2"]`, and `"endings": false`; in `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/seed-3760-v0.4.12c.json`, add `"start": "plain"` and `"endings": true`. These are the values drawn by their historical setup streams. In each `found`, remove only the obsolete sentence saying regress plays another/plain game; keep seeds, versions, decks, and failure evidence unchanged. These are real failures, not manufactured corpus evidence.
6. In `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md`, expand the field table with every new optional field and its exact JSON spelling, state that absent fields preserve legacy plain/no-channel replay, explain that reports print the fields to copy, distinguish ordinary versus run deck-size linting, and say board ids (including every ingredient of a fused id) are retired rather than edited when no longer rebuildable. Replace the final plain-start limitation with the pinned unhandicapped-1v1 scope; keep handicapped-wave and Duos records explicitly out of scope. In `crates/tools/README.md`, change the `fuzz --regress` clause from “pinned decks” to pinned decks, literal start inputs, and endings-channel choice.

## Tests

- In `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`'s `fuzz_regression_corpus` module, update `sound` for the defaulted fields and extend `a_corpus_file_of_the_wrong_shape_does_not_parse` to prove a legacy JSON record omitting all new fields parses as plain/no-channel and unknown fields remain rejected.
- Extend `the_lint_passes_a_sound_record_and_names_each_malformed_one` with exact cases for mismatched start/input fields, invalid dealt seats, out-of-range run deck lengths, invalid deck marks/handicaps, and a missing catalog id in a plain or fused board; also assert a retired record with that missing board id lints clean without editing it.
- Replace `a_corpus_record_replays_from_the_plain_start_whatever_start_its_seed_draws` with `a_corpus_record_replays_its_pinned_last_boards`: choose a seed whose live draw differs, pin a small literal `lastBoards` value, and assert `Passed.start == StartKind::LastBoards`, deterministic repeat, and a different hash from the same decks replayed plain; this fails if replay merely redraws or ignores the boards. Add `a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag`, loading seed 3760's checked-in decks, calling `play_game_with_options`, and asserting its `endings: true` log contains an action the policy never sends while the otherwise identical false record's log does not.
- Add `a_failure_prints_copy_pasteable_pinned_corpus_fields`, and extend `a_run_failure_prints_its_handicaps_and_marks_in_the_report_and_the_json`, to assert the exact JSON field names and literal dealt, board, run, and true/false endings values in the text report while preserving existing JSON output. Keep `a_failure_names_its_start_in_the_report_and_the_json_and_the_summary_counts_every_start` passing unchanged apart from the new `Failure.endings` fixture field.
- In `the_checked_in_corpus_lints_clean_and_every_record_replays`, additionally locate seed 8 and seed 3760: assert seed 8 parses as `StartKind::Dealt`, `dealt == [P1, P2]`, and `endings == false`, and seed 3760 as `StartKind::Plain` with `endings == true`; replay both and assert seed 8's `Passed.start == StartKind::Dealt`.
- Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fuzz_regression_corpus`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools a_corpus_record_replays_its_pinned_last_boards`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools a_failure_prints_copy_pasteable_pinned_corpus_fields`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools a_run_failure_prints_its_handicaps_and_marks_in_the_report_and_the_json`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, and `cargo jackioh spec check`. Do not run the full workspace, full fuzz wave, or other prohibited whole suites.

## Done when

- [ ] Legacy corpus JSON defaults to the same plain start and all existing live records pass.
- [ ] A pinned dealt/board/run record uses its literal start inputs for creation, replay fold, and checkpoint; endings-channel playback follows the pinned flag.
- [ ] Run decks accept only the configured dungeon range, normal/legacy decks retain their current sizes, and invalid handicaps/marks are lint errors.
- [ ] A catalog id removed from a pinned board requires `retired` and no record data is rewritten.
- [ ] Failure text prints record-ready start fields and the README documents them and the 1v1-only scope.
- [ ] The seed-8 historical dealt failure is replayed from both dealt seats.
- [ ] The seed-3760 historical failure is replayed with its endings channel.
- [ ] Targeted tests, tools crate tests/clippy, rustfmt, catalog, patches, and spec checks pass.

## Risks

- Redrawing boards from a seed would still drift with the catalog; store and replay the serialized `LastBoardInput` verbatim, validating fused ingredients through `rebuildable_from_id`.
- Creation, full-log fold, and checkpoint-prefix fold can diverge if they build options separately; construct one pinned options shape and use the same fields for all three paths.
- `create_recorded_game` is required for 20-card legacy records and run handicap sizes; do not route corpus options through new-game validation.
- The corpus is only the unhandicapped 1v1 stream. Do not infer support for the handicap-prefixed policy streams or Duos from the presence of dungeon `handicaps`.
- Avoid changing public engine/wire types or the existing `--json` report contract; corpus fields are tooling-only serde data.

## Open questions

None. Existing seed-8 and seed-3760 records supply real evidence for the non-plain and endings fixtures, fixing their documented replay mismatches without inventing a failure.

Add `play_game_with_options`, `check_replay_with_options`, `check_serial_restart_with_options`, and `run_seed_with_options` beside their current functions: the current functions remain wrappers that call `GameSetup::create_options`, while `replay_record` creates a `GameSetup` with `recorded: true`, `start: record.start`, and `endings: record.endings`, then calls `run_seed_with_options` with `record.create_options()`.
